• The sources of Vitamin D are - Egg, liver, dairy products, Fish, synthesized by the skin in sunlight.

questions.q_en: What is the name of the inflammatory condition that causes cracks, crusting and scaling at the corners of the mouth due to vitamin B2 deficiency?
questions.solution_en: The correct answer is Cheilosis. This condition, also known as angular cheilitis, is caused by a deficiency of vitamin B2 (riboflavin) and leads to painful cracks, redness, and scaling at the corners of the mouth.

questions.q_en: What is pro-vitamin A or the anti-cancer compound present in carrots called?
questions.solution_en:
Beta-carotene is a prominent carotenoid pigment found in carrots and other orange, yellow, and dark green leafy vegetables and fruits. It is a pro-vitamin A, meaning the human body can convert it into vitamin A (retinol). Beta-carotene is also known for its antioxidant properties, which contribute to its potential anti-cancer effects.

Explanation of Other Options:

• Alpha-resins: Resins are complex chemical compounds, often found in plant exudates. Alpha-resins (like humulones) are specific compounds found in hops, contributing to the bitterness of beer, not the pro-vitamin A in carrots.

• Delta-terpenes: Terpenes are a large and diverse class of organic compounds produced by a variety of plants. While carotenoids (like beta-carotene) are tetraterpenoids, "delta-terpenes" is not a specific well-known pro-vitamin A compound in carrots.

• Alpha-terpenoid: Terpenoids (or isoprenoids) are a class of naturally occurring organic chemicals derived from isoprene. Beta-carotene is a terpenoid, but "alpha-terpenoid" is a general classification, not the specific name of the pro-vitamin A compound in carrots.

Further insights:

• Vitamin A is essential for vision, immune function, cell growth, and reproduction.

• Carotenoids like beta-carotene, alpha-carotene, and beta-cryptoxanthin are precursors to vitamin A.

• The antioxidant properties of beta-carotene help protect cells from damage caused by free radicals, which may play a role in cancer development.

questions.q_en:
Which of the following statements about nutrients are correct?

Statement A: C, H, O, N, P and K are macro nutrients.

Statement B: Fe, Mn, Ni, Co and Mo are micronutrients.

Statement C: Micronutrients are not essential for our body.
options_en: All statements A, B and C
questions.solution_en:
• Micronutrients are essential; hence Statement C is incorrect.

• Macronutrients are the nutrients required by the body in large amounts for energy and growth.

• Micronutrients are the nutrients needed by the body in small amounts for proper functioning of enzymes, hormones, and other body processes.

questions.q_en: What are the five Fs of indirect transmission?
options_en: Flies, fingers, fomites, food and fluid
Fruit, fingers, flu, food and fluid
Flies, fingers, friends, food and fruit
Flies, fingers, fomites, food and fruit
questions.solution_en: In epidemiology, the five Fs represent the primary routes of indirect disease transmission. These include: Flies (insects that transport pathogens), Fingers (contaminated hands), Fomites (inanimate objects carrying pathogens), Food (contaminated food items), and Fluid (contaminated water or other liquids). This concept is fundamental in understanding disease transmission and implementing preventive measures.

questions.q_en:
Which of the following options is correct regarding sexually transmitted disease (STD)?

Statement A: Sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) are infections transmitted from an infected person to an uninfected person through sexual contact.

Statement B: HIV, HPV and Hepatitis B virus is responsible for STD.
options_en: Both Statements A and B incorrect
Both Statements A and B correct
questions.solution_en: Sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) are infections transmitted from an infected person to an uninfected person through sexual contact. STDs can be caused by bacteria, viruses, or parasites. Examples include gonorrhea, genital herpes, human papilloma virus infection, HIV/AIDS, chlamydia, and syphilis.

questions.q_en: Which of the following is a rare group of genetic disorders caused by mutations of certain genes affecting the colour (pigmentation) of the skin, hair and eyes?
questions.solution_en:
• Albinism is a rare genetic disorder caused by mutations in genes that affect the production of melanin, the pigment responsible for the color of the skin, hair, and eyes.

• Individuals with albinism have little to no melanin, resulting in pale skin, white or light-colored hair, and often vision problems due to a lack of pigmentation in the eyes.

Other Options Explained:

• Alkaptonuria: A rare inherited disorder that leads to the buildup of homogentisic acid in the body, causing darkening of the urine and eventually leading to arthritis and other symptoms. It does not affect pigmentation.

• Alagille syndrome: A genetic disorder that affects several parts of the body, especially the liver, heart, and skeleton, but does not primarily affect pigmentation.

• Angelman syndrome: A neurogenetic disorder characterized by developmental delay, speech impairment, movement or balance disorders, and sometimes seizures. It is not related to pigmentation.

Further Insight:

• Types of Albinism: There are different forms, including ocular albinism (affecting the eyes), cutaneous albinism (affecting skin and hair), and oculocutaneous albinism (affecting both).

questions.q_en: Which of the following is a disease caused by drinking contaminated water?
questions.solution_en: Cholera is an acute diarrheal illness caused by infection of the intestine with Vibrio cholera bacteria. People can get sick when they swallow food or water contaminated with cholera bacteria. The infection is often mild or without symptoms, but can sometimes be severe and life-threatening.
